1-2.word_for_word: dvitīye — in the second chapter; kaṃsa-ghātāya — for the killing of Kaṃsa; devakyā garbha-gaḥ hariḥ — Hari entering the womb of Devakī; brahmādibhiḥ stutaḥ — praised by Brahmā and the other gods; sā ca sāntvitā — and Devakī is comforted; yadubhiḥ sa vyarudhyata iti uktam — it was previously said that Kaṃsa became hostile to the Yadus; tam eva virodham prapañcayati — that same hostility is now expanded; devakī-garbhasya anyatra sañcāreṇa — through the transfer of Devakī’s embryo elsewhere; bhagavataḥ praveśam vaktum — in order to narrate Bhagavān’s entrance; pralamba-ity-ādi-sārdha-śloka-trayeṇa — by the three-and-a-half verses beginning with ‘Pralamba’; mahāśanaḥ — the one called Mahāśana; aghāsuraḥ — Aghāsura.
1-2.translation: In the second chapter it is described that Hari enters Devakī’s womb for the destruction of Kaṃsa, is praised by Brahmā and the other gods, and that Devakī is comforted. It was previously said that Kaṃsa became hostile to the Yadus. That same hostility is now elaborated in the three-and-a-half verses beginning with ‘Pralamba,’ so that the narrative may quickly proceed to the transfer of Devakī’s embryo elsewhere and Bhagavān’s entrance into her womb. ‘Mahāśana’ refers to Aghāsura.

4.word_for_word: anurundhānāḥ — complying with him, accommodating his wishes, acting in accordance with him.
4.translation: ‘Anurundhānāḥ’ means those who complied with Kaṃsa and acted in accordance with his wishes.

5.word_for_word: dhāma — a potency or portion; kalā — a plenary portion; tat eva saptamaḥ garbhaḥ babhūva — that very potency became the seventh embryo; yam anantam iti — the one whom they call Ananta; harṣa-śoka-vivardhanaḥ — increasing both joy and grief; ānanda-rūpasya avatīrṇatvāt harṣaḥ — joy because one whose nature is bliss had descended; pūrva-garbha-sādhāraṇa-dṛṣṭyā ca śokaḥ — grief because she viewed him under the same danger as the previous embryos.
5.translation: ‘Dhāma’ here means a potency or plenary portion: that very potency became Devakī’s seventh embryo, the one known as Ananta. He increased both her joy and her grief—joy because one whose very nature is bliss had descended, and grief because, when she regarded this pregnancy like the previous ones, she feared the same fate for the child.

7.word_for_word: sā gokule kim iti āste — why is Rohiṇī staying in Gokula?; anyāś ca — ‘and the others’; na kevalam sā eva — not she alone; anyā api — other wives also; vivareṣu — in hidden places; alakṣya-sthāneṣu — in places where they would not be noticed.
7.translation: One may ask why Rohiṇī was staying in Gokula. The words ‘and the others’ answer this: she was not the only one. Other wives of Vasudeva, frightened by Kaṃsa, were also living in concealed places where they would not be noticed.

8.word_for_word: jaṭhare santam — the embryo already present in Devakī’s womb; garbhaḥ ākṛṣyamāṇaḥ katham jīvet — how could an embryo survive while being drawn out and transferred?; māmakaṃ dhāma — ‘My own dhāma,’ My own potency or manifestation.
8.translation: The embryo is already present in Devakī’s womb. If one asks how an embryo could remain alive while being drawn out and transferred, the answer lies in the expression ‘My own dhāma’: this embryo is the Lord’s own potency or manifestation.

9.word_for_word: kim-artham evam kāryam — why must this be done?; atha — immediately afterward; aṃśa-bhāgena — by/with the aṃśa-bhāga; aṃśaiḥ śaktibhiḥ adhi-tiṣṭhati sarvān brahmādi-stamba-paryantān — He pervades all beings from Brahmā down to a blade of grass through His potencies; paripūrṇena rūpeṇa — in the completely full form; aṃśaiḥ jñāna-aiśvarya-balādibhiḥ bhājayati svīyān — He endows His own with portions such as knowledge, sovereignty and strength; aṃśena puruṣa-rūpeṇa — through the Puruṣa form as an aṃśa; māyāyā bhāgaḥ īkṣaṇam yasya — whose relation to Māyā is His glance upon her; aṃśena māyayā — with Māyā as a potency; guṇāvatārādi-rūpā bhāgā bhedā yasya — whose divisions include the guṇāvatāras and other forms; aṃśā matsya-kūrmādi-rūpā bhajanīyāḥ — whose aṃśas such as Matsya and Kūrma are worshipable; na tu sākṣāt-svarūpam — while His own immediate form is not merely an aṃśa; sarvathā paripūrṇena rūpeṇa — in every interpretation the intention is His completely full form; kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam — because ‘Kṛṣṇa alone is Bhagavān Himself.’
9.translation: Why is this transfer to be carried out? ‘Atha’ means that immediately afterward the Lord Himself will appear. Śrīdhara gives several possible analyses of ‘aṃśa-bhāgena’: He pervades beings from Brahmā down to a blade of grass through His potencies; He endows His own with portions of knowledge, sovereignty and strength; the Puruṣa is His aṃśa whose relation to Māyā is through the glance; Māyā and the guṇāvatāras may be described as dependent portions or divisions; and forms such as Matsya and Kūrma are worshipable aṃśas while Kṛṣṇa’s immediate form is not merely a portion. The point of these explanations, Śrīdhara says, is that Kṛṣṇa appears here in His completely full form, in accord with ‘Kṛṣṇas tu Bhagavān svayam.’

10.word_for_word: sarvān putrādīn kāmayante ye — those who desire objects such as sons; teṣām varām īśvarīm — for them, the excellent sovereign goddess; śreṣṭhām niyantrīm — the supreme controller; arcakānām sarvān kāma-varān pradadāti yā — she who grants all desired boons to her worshipers.
10.translation: She is the excellent sovereign goddess of those who desire boons such as sons: the supreme controller who grants all desired blessings to her worshipers. Śrīdhara marks this explanation as applying through verses 10–12.

11-12.word_for_word: na pṛthak vyākhyātam — no separate additional explanation is given here; pūrva-vyākhyā 10-12 iti aṅkitā — the preceding gloss on verse 10 is explicitly marked by Śrīdhara as extending through verses 10–12.
11-12.translation: No separate additional explanation is given under these two verses. Śrīdhara explicitly marks his preceding gloss on verse 10 as covering verses 10 through 12.

13.word_for_word: tvad-vikrameṇa — through this action or power; bhūvi — in the world; taṃ vai saṅkarṣaṇaṃ prāhuḥ — they call him Saṅkarṣaṇa; loka-ramaṇāt — because he delights the people; rāma iti — therefore ‘Rāma’; bala-ucchrayāt — because of the eminence of strength; balabhadraṃ prāhuḥ — therefore ‘Balabhadra.’
13.translation: Through this act of transfer he is known in the world as Saṅkarṣaṇa. Because he delights the people he is called Rāma, and because of his preeminent strength he is called Balabhadra.

14.word_for_word: tathā iti — saying ‘so be it’; punaḥ api om iti — and again saying ‘om’; ādareṇa pratigṛhya — respectfully accepting the command; gām — the earth; pṛthvīm — the terrestrial world.
14.translation: She respectfully accepted Bhagavān’s command with ‘So be it’ and again with the solemn assent ‘om’; then she went to the earth.

15.word_for_word: visraṃsitaḥ — slipped away; vibhraṣṭaḥ — fallen or miscarried; visrastaḥ — lost; iti vicukruśuḥ — thus the townspeople cried out; na tu tat viduḥ — but they did not know what had actually happened.
15.translation: ‘Visraṃsita’ means that the embryo had slipped away, fallen or been lost. The townspeople cried out that Devakī had miscarried, but they did not know what had actually happened.

16.word_for_word: manaḥ āviveśa — He entered the mind; manasi āvirbabhūva — He manifested within Vasudeva’s mind; jīvānām iva na dhātu-sambandhaḥ — there was no physical connection with reproductive elements as with ordinary living beings.
16.translation: ‘He entered Vasudeva’s mind’ means that Bhagavān manifested within his mind. There was no connection with physical reproductive elements as there is in the generation of ordinary embodied beings.

17.word_for_word: dhāma — the radiant manifestation; śrī-mūrtim — the auspicious divine form.
17.translation: Here ‘dhāma’ means the Lord’s radiant, auspicious divine form.

18.word_for_word: jagan-maṅgalam — the embodied auspiciousness of the world; acyuta-aṃśam — one whose aṃśas or excellences are unfailing; yad vā acyutasya aṃśa iva — or appearing like a portion of Acyuta; bhaktānām anugrahārtham paricchinna-vapuḥ — assuming a bounded visible form for the grace of devotees; samyak-bhūtam eva āhitam — truly and fully placed; vaidha-dīkṣayā arpitam — imparted as by a mental initiation; devī — the shining one, pure sattva; sarvātmakaṃ — the Self of all; ātma-bhūtam — already belonging to her innermost self; manastaḥ manasā eva dadhāra — she bore Him by mental reception; yathā kāṣṭhā prācī dik ānanda-karam candram — like the eastern quarter bearing the joy-giving moon.
18.translation: ‘The auspiciousness of the world’ means auspiciousness itself embodied for the whole world. ‘Acyutāṃśa’ can indicate His unfailing plenitude, or His appearing like a portion of Acyuta by assuming a visible form for the grace of devotees. Vasudeva had truly placed Him in Devakī through a transmission compared to mental initiation. Devakī is called ‘devī’ because she is radiant and of pure sattva. She bore within herself the One who is the Self of all and who was already present as her innermost Self, receiving Him through the mind. The comparison is the eastern horizon bearing the joy-giving moon.

19.word_for_word: sarva-jagan-nivāsasya śrī-hareḥ — of Śrī Hari, the abode of the entire universe; nivāsa-bhūtā satī api — although she had become His abode; nitarām sarva-jana-āhlādakatayā na reje — she did not shine openly so as to delight everyone; svayam eva ānandam anvabhavat — rather she herself experienced the bliss; kaṃsasya gṛhe ruddhā — confined in Kaṃsa’s house; anyaiḥ na dṛśyate — she was not seen by others; ruddhā agni-śikhā iva — like an enclosed lamp-flame; sarasvatī jñāna-khale ruddhā yathā — like learning confined in one who withholds or falsifies knowledge; anyeṣām anupakāriṇī — of no benefit to others.
19.translation: Although Devakī had become the dwelling place of Śrī Hari, who is Himself the dwelling place of the entire universe, she did not shine openly so as to delight everyone; rather, she herself experienced that bliss. Confined in Kaṃsa’s house, she was hidden from others, like a lamp-flame enclosed within a vessel. Śrīdhara gives a second comparison: learning confined in one who hoards or falsifies knowledge does not benefit others; so too Devakī’s splendor was not yet available to the world.

20.word_for_word: prabhayā bhavanaṃ virocayantīm — illuminating the house with her radiance; ajitaḥ antarā — Ajita, the unconquered Lord, was within; kukṣi-madhye — in the midst of her womb; eṣa virocamānaḥ dhruvaṃ hariḥ eva — this radiance is certainly Hari Himself; īdṛśī iyaṃ purā na āsīt — she had never been like this before.
20.translation: Kaṃsa saw Devakī illuminating the house with her radiance, with Ajita, the unconquered Lord, within her womb. He concluded: ‘This brilliance is certainly Hari Himself, because she was never like this before.’

21.word_for_word: santi sāma-ādayaḥ upāyāḥ — there are means such as conciliation; ayam artha-tantraḥ deva-kārya-pradhānaḥ — this Lord is intent upon the divine objective; vikramaṃ na vihanti — He will not abandon His prowess; mad-vadhe parākramaṃ kariṣyati eva — He will certainly exercise His power in killing me; yad vā — alternatively; idānīm eva iyaṃ hanyatām — ‘let her be killed now’; artha-tantraḥ api pumān svaṃ vikramaṃ na vihanti — even a self-interested man does not destroy his own reputation for valor; strī-vadhe tat-nāśaḥ syāt — killing a woman would destroy that valor/reputation; guru-matyāḥ — of a pregnant woman, one heavy with child.
21.translation: Kaṃsa considers whether another expedient such as conciliation might work, but rejects it: the Lord is intent upon the divine purpose and will certainly use His power to kill him. Śrīdhara then gives another reading. If Kaṃsa thinks, ‘Then I should kill her immediately,’ he reflects that even a man pursuing his own interest does not destroy his own reputation for valor; killing a woman—especially his own pregnant sister—would do exactly that. ‘Guru-matyā’ means a woman heavy with child.

22.word_for_word: sa eṣa jīvan api mṛtaḥ syāt — such a man, though living, would be as good as dead; nṛśaṃsitena — through cruelty; yaḥ varteta — one who lives that way; taṃ jīvantam eva manujāḥ śapanti — people curse him even while alive; dur-vākyaiḥ dhik-kurvanti — they condemn him with harsh words; dehe mṛte — when the body dies; tanu-māninaḥ pāpinaḥ — the sinful person attached to bodily self-interest; narakaṃ gacchati — goes to hell; dhruvam andhaṃ tamaḥ gamiṣyati — ‘he will certainly go to blinding darkness.’
22.translation: A person who lives by extreme cruelty is, even while alive, as good as dead: people curse him and condemn him with harsh words. When his body dies, the sinful person who clings to bodily self-interest goes to hell. Alternatively, the last words may be understood as the very form of the people’s curse: ‘When this body is dead, he will certainly go to blinding darkness.’

24.word_for_word: saṃviśan — lying down, reclining; śayānaḥ — lying or sleeping.
24.translation: ‘Saṃviśan’ means ‘lying down.’ In every posture and activity Kaṃsa remained absorbed in thought of Hṛṣīkeśa.

25.word_for_word: ramyābhiḥ gīrbhiḥ — with beautiful words or hymns; vṛṣaṇam — the bestower of desires; kāma-varṣiṇam — showering desired blessings; aiḍayan — they praised; tuṣṭuvuḥ — they offered hymns of praise.
25.translation: With beautiful words the gods praised Him as ‘vṛṣaṇa,’ the one who showers desired blessings; that is, they offered Him hymns of praise.

26.word_for_word: pratiśrutaṃ satyaṃ kṛtam iti hṛṣṭāḥ — joyful that the promised word had been made true; satyatvena eva prathamaṃ stuvanti — they first praise Him as Truth; satya-vratam — one whose vow or resolve is true; satya-param — in whom truth is supreme, the highest means of attainment; tri-satyam — true in the three times; sṛṣṭeḥ pūrvaṃ — before creation; pralaya-antaram — through dissolution; sthiti-samaye — during maintenance; satyasya yonim — the source of the five elements denoted by sat and tyat; sat — earth, water and fire; tyat — air and ether; satye nihitam — present within that reality as Inner Controller; satyasya satyam — the reality of that reality, remaining unchanged when it is destroyed; ṛta-satya-netram — the guide of ṛta and satya; ṛtam — truthful, gracious speech; satyam — equal vision; satyātmakam — whose nature is truth; tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prapannāḥ — we have taken refuge in You.
26.translation: The gods are joyful that the Lord has made His promise true, so they begin by praising Him as Truth. ‘Satya-vrata’ means that His resolve is unfailingly true. ‘Satya-param’ indicates that truth is supreme in Him and is the highest means of reaching Him. He is ‘tri-satya,’ true in all three times—before creation, throughout cosmic existence and through dissolution. He is the source of the five elements, here denoted by ‘sat’ and ‘tyat’; He is also present within them as the Inner Controller, and when they perish He remains as ‘the truth of the true,’ unchanged. ‘Ṛta’ is truthful, gracious speech and ‘satya’ is equal vision; He is their guide and impeller. Thus, being truth in every way, He is the one in whom the gods take refuge.

27.word_for_word: tvam eva ekaḥ sarveśvaraḥ — You alone are the Lord of all; sarva-sṛṣṭy-ādi-kāraṇatvāt — because You are the cause of creation and all that follows; vayam tu tvad-eka-śaraṇāḥ — we have You alone as refuge; dvaita-prapañcaṃ vṛkṣa-rūpakeṇa nirūpayanti — they describe the manifold world as a tree; ādi-vṛkṣaḥ — the primordial world-tree; samasṭi-vyaṣṭi-deha-rūpaḥ — collective and individual bodies; ekāyanaḥ — having one basis, Prakṛti; dve phale — two fruits, pleasure and pain; trayo mūlāni — three roots, the guṇas; catvāro rasāḥ — four tastes, dharma, artha, kāma and mokṣa; pañca indriyāṇi vidhāḥ — five modes through the senses; ṣaḍ ūrmayaḥ koṣā vā — six waves or sheaths; sapta dhātavaḥ tvacaḥ — seven bodily constituents; aṣṭau viṭapāḥ — eight branches, the five elements plus mind, intellect and ego; nava dvārāṇi — nine openings; daśa prāṇāḥ — ten vital airs; dvau jīva-īśvarau khagau — two birds, the individual self and the Lord.
27.translation: The implied objection is: ‘You too are rulers of worlds; why do you take refuge in Me?’ The gods answer that the Lord alone is the Supreme Lord because He is the ultimate cause of creation and all that follows, while they depend entirely upon Him. They then describe the world as a tree. Its one ground is Prakṛti; its two fruits are pleasure and pain; its three roots are the three guṇas; its four tastes are dharma, artha, kāma and mokṣa; its five modes are the five senses; its six waves or sheaths are dispositions of embodied existence; its seven coverings are the bodily constituents; its eight branches are the five elements together with mind, intellect and ego; its nine openings are the bodily gates; its ten leaves are the vital airs; and the two birds dwelling in it are the individual self and the Lord.

28.word_for_word: saṃsāra-vṛkṣasya sataḥ kāryasya — of the world-tree just described, an existent effect; tvam eka eva prasūtiḥ — You alone are its source; kāraṇam — the cause; tvam eva sannidhānam — You alone are its resting place; laya-sthānam — the place of dissolution; tvam eva anugrahaḥ — You alone are its protection; pālakaḥ — the maintainer; brahma-viṣṇu-rudrāḥ evam-bhūtāḥ prasiddhāḥ — Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra are commonly regarded as these agents; tvat-māyayā saṃvṛta-cetasaḥ — those whose understanding is covered by Your Māyā; tvām eva nānā paśyanti — see You alone as many; vipascitaḥ tathā na paśyanti — the wise do not see You as ultimately divided.
28.translation: Of the world-tree just described, You alone are the source from which it is born, the resting place into which it dissolves and the protector who maintains it. If one objects that Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra are commonly regarded as distinct agents of these functions, the answer is that minds covered by Your Māyā see the one Lord as many. The wise do not regard You as ultimately divided.

29.word_for_word: avabodha-eka-svarūpaḥ ātmā — the Self whose nature is pure awareness; tvam eva rūpāṇi mūrtīḥ bibharṣi — You Yourself assume these forms; na tu tvaṃ kasyāpi putraḥ — You are not truly dependent on being anyone’s son; kṣemāya pālanāya — for welfare, protection and preservation; satāṃ dharma-vartināṃ sukha-karāṇi — Your forms bring happiness to the righteous; khalānām abhadrāṇi nāśakāni — they destroy the inauspicious power of the wicked.
29.translation: You are the Self whose nature is pure awareness, and You Yourself assume these forms; in truth You are not dependent on being anyone’s son. You bear such forms for the welfare and protection of the moving and nonmoving world. They bring happiness to the righteous and repeatedly destroy the inauspicious power of the wicked.

30.word_for_word: bhaktānāṃ mokṣārtham api — also for the liberation of devotees; tvayi samādhinā āveśita-cetasā — with the mind absorbed in You through samādhi; tvat-pāda-potena — by the boat of Your feet; eke — the foremost discerning devotees; mahadbhiḥ kṛtena — made serviceable or highly esteemed by the great souls; bhava-abdhiṃ tucchī-kurvanti — they make the ocean of becoming insignificant; anāyāsena eva bhajana-anu-niṣpādinī muktiḥ — liberation follows their devotion effortlessly.
30.translation: The Lord’s forms are not only for protecting the world; they also serve the liberation of devotees. The foremost discerning devotees absorb their minds in Him through samādhi and take shelter of the boat of His feet, honored and made accessible by the great souls. In this way they reduce the ocean of material becoming to something as insignificant as a calf’s hoof-print. Liberation follows their devotion without separate labor.

31.word_for_word: tena potena pūrve cet pāraṃ gatāḥ — if earlier saints crossed by that boat; idānīntanānāṃ kā gatiḥ — what is the way for people now?; he dyuman — O self-luminous Lord; tvat-pāda-pota-sāmīpya-mātreṇa — merely by nearness to the boat of Your feet; bhava-ambudhau vatsa-pada-mātre jāte — when the ocean of becoming has become only a calf’s hoof-print; bhavārṇavaṃ samuttīrya — having crossed the terrible ocean; bhavat-pada-amboruha-rūpāṃ nāvam atra eva nidhāya — leaving here the boat that is Your lotus feet; bhakti-mārga-sampradāyaṃ pravartya — establishing and transmitting the path of bhakti; adabhra-sauhṛdāḥ — possessing immense friendship and compassion; sarva-bhūteṣu ati-prīti-yuktāḥ — deeply loving toward all beings; sad-anugrahaḥ bhavān — You bestow grace upon the devotees.
31.translation: If the saints of former times crossed by the boat of the Lord’s feet, what remains for people now? Śrīdhara explains that merely approaching that boat makes the ocean of becoming shrink to a calf’s hoof-print. The great devotees crossed that terrible ocean themselves, yet did not take the boat away: they left the lotus feet of the Lord here by establishing and transmitting the path of bhakti. Because their compassion for all beings is immense, they left that way for others; and because the Lord bestows grace upon His devotees, even approaching that boat is effective.

32.word_for_word: vimukta-māninaḥ — those who imagine themselves liberated; vimuktā vayam iti manyamānāḥ — thinking ‘we are liberated’; tvayi nirastaḥ bhāvaḥ — whose disposition toward You has been set aside; bhakteḥ abhāvāt — because devotion is absent; aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ — their intelligence is not purified; yad vā tvayi asta-bhāḥ — alternatively, their light/intelligence is extinguished with regard to You; vādeṣu eva viśuddha-buddhayaḥ — their intelligence is refined only in argument; kṛcchreṇa — with great difficulty; paraṃ padam — a high station near liberation; patanti — they fall, overcome by obstacles; anādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ — because they have not honored Your feet.
32.translation: Those who merely imagine themselves liberated are not truly purified, because devotion toward You is absent or rejected. Alternatively, their intelligence may be sharp only in philosophical argument while remaining dark toward You. After great difficulty and austerity over many births they may reach an elevated condition close to liberation, yet they fall when obstacles overpower them because they have not honored Your feet.

33.word_for_word: tvadīyāḥ tu na kadācit api patanti — Your own devotees never fall; vināyakāḥ — causes of obstruction; vighna-hetavaḥ — obstacles; teṣām anīkāni — their hosts or armies; teṣāṃ mūrdhasu vicaranti — Your devotees move over their heads; vighnān jayanti — that is, they conquer the obstacles.
33.translation: Your own devotees, by contrast, never fall. ‘Vināyakas’ are causes of obstruction and their ‘hosts’ are masses of obstacles. Protected by You, Your devotees are said to walk over the heads of their leaders—that is, they conquer those obstacles and proceed without fear.

34.word_for_word: satāṃ sukhāvahāni rūpāṇi dhārayasi iti uktam — it was said that You assume forms bringing happiness to the good; sattvaṃ viśuddham — pure sattva; vapuḥ āśrayate bhavān — You assume a form of pure sattva; śreya-upāyanam — bringing the highest good; yena vapuṣā janaḥ tava arhaṇam īhate — through that form people undertake Your worship; vedāḥ ca kriyā-yogāḥ ca tapaḥ ca samādhiḥ ca — through Vedic practice, sacred action, austerity and samādhi; vapuṣaḥ anāśrayaṇe arhaṇa-asambhavāt — without Your assuming such a form, worship could not occur; na karma-phala-siddhiḥ syāt — the intended fruits of sacred action could not be fulfilled.
34.translation: It was said that the Lord assumes forms that bring happiness to the righteous; this verse explains how. He assumes a form of pure sattva, a form that brings the highest good. Through that manifest form people can worship Him by the Vedas, sacred acts, austerity and samādhi. If He did not make Himself available in such a form, worship could not be directed toward Him and the promised fruits of sacred practice could not be realized.

35.word_for_word: bhagavad-bhaktānām eva mokṣaḥ na anyeṣām iti uktam — the preceding verses said that liberation belongs to devotees of Bhagavān; mokṣasya jñāna-eka-sādhyatvāt kim bhaktyā — objection: if liberation is attained by knowledge alone, why bhakti?; idam sattvaṃ nijaṃ tava vapuḥ — this pure sattva is Your own intrinsic form; na bhavet cet — if it did not manifest; vijñānam viśiṣṭam aparokṣam jñānam na bhavet — there would be no distinct direct realization; ajñānam ca tat-kṛtā bhidā ca tayoḥ apamārjanam — it removes ignorance and the distinctions produced by ignorance; guṇa-prakāśaiḥ — through manifestations limited by the guṇas; bhavān sarva-sākṣī paripūrṇaḥ kevalam anumīyate — You, the complete Witness of all, can only be inferred; na tu sākṣātkriyate — not directly realized; śuddha-sattva-vapuṣi tvayi sevyamāne — when You in Your pure-sattva form are served; tvat-prasādena sākṣātkāraḥ bhavet — direct realization arises by Your grace.
35.translation: The preceding verses said that devotees of Bhagavān attain liberation. One may object: if liberation is achieved by knowledge, what need is there for bhakti? Śrīdhara answers that if the Lord’s own pure-sattva form did not manifest, there could be no distinct, direct realization that removes ignorance and the separations produced by ignorance. From ordinary manifestations conditioned by the guṇas one can only infer the complete Witness of all; one does not thereby directly see Him. When the Lord’s own pure-sattva form is served, however, direct realization arises by His grace.

36.word_for_word: bhaktānām abhyudaya-apavargārtham rūpāṇi bibharti — He assumes forms for devotees’ welfare and liberation; tāni bhajanīyāni — those forms are to be worshiped; na tu jñātuṃ śakyante — they cannot be completely comprehended; anantatvāt — because they are infinite; atarkyatvāt — beyond reasoning; mano-vacasoḥ agocaratvāt — beyond mind and speech; nāma-rūpe guṇa-janma-karmabhiḥ nirūpaṇa-arhe na bhavataḥ — His name and form cannot be exhaustively defined by qualities, births and deeds; tasya sākṣiṇaḥ — because He is the Witness; na hi sākṣiṇaḥ tattvaṃ mano-vaco-gocaram — the truth of the Witness is not an object of mind or speech; atha api kriyāyām — nevertheless, in worship and contemplative practice; tvāṃ pratiyanti — worshipers directly realize You.
36.translation: The Lord assumes forms for the welfare and liberation of devotees, but those forms are objects of worship, not objects finite thought can exhaustively comprehend. Because the Lord is infinite, beyond reasoning and beyond the reach of mind and speech, His names and forms cannot be completely delimited by descriptions of qualities, births and deeds. As the Witness, His essential nature cannot itself become an ordinary object of thought or speech. Nevertheless, through acts of worship and contemplative practice, devotees directly realize Him.

37.word_for_word: tasmāt bhaktyā eva mokṣaḥ — therefore liberation is by bhakti alone; śṛṇvan — hearing; gṛṇan — chanting or speaking; saṃsmarayan — repeatedly remembering and reminding others; cintayan — contemplating; kriyāsu — in sacred acts; devārcanādi-karmasu — in activities such as deity worship; tvat-caraṇāravindayoḥ āviṣṭa-cetāḥ — with the mind absorbed in Your lotus feet; na bhavāya kalpate — is not destined for material becoming or rebirth.
37.translation: The gods conclude that liberation is attained through bhakti. One who hears, chants, repeatedly remembers and contemplates the Lord’s auspicious names and forms, and whose mind remains absorbed in His lotus feet while performing acts such as deity worship, is no longer destined for material becoming.

38.word_for_word: viśeṣataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-avatāram abhinandanti — they especially rejoice in Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s descent; diṣṭyā — by good fortune; tava janma-mātreṇa bhuvaḥ bhāraḥ apanītaḥ — merely by Your birth the burden of earth is removed; tvat-padakaiḥ — by Your tender footsteps; komalaiḥ padaiḥ — soft feet; suśobhanaiḥ vajra-aṅkuśādi-śubha-lakṣaṇaiḥ — beautifully marked with auspicious signs such as the thunderbolt and goad; gām pṛthvīṃ — the earth; dyāṃ svargaṃ ca — and heaven; tvayā anukampitām — favored by Your compassion; drakṣyāma — we shall behold.
38.translation: The gods now rejoice specifically in Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s descent. By great good fortune, the burden of the earth is already removed simply by the Lord’s birth. They look forward to seeing the earth beautified by His soft feet, marked with auspicious signs such as the thunderbolt and goad, and to seeing both earth and heaven favored by His compassion.

39.word_for_word: tava janmanā bhāraḥ apanītaḥ iti uktyā — after saying that the earth’s burden is removed by Your birth; mama api kim jīva-vat saṃsāraḥ uktaḥ — objection: does this imply Your birth is saṃsāra like a jīva’s?; na hi — certainly not; he īśa — O Lord; asaṃsāriṇaḥ te janmanaḥ kāraṇam — for You, beyond saṃsāra, there is no compulsory cause of birth; krīḍāṃ vinā na tarkayāmaḥ — we conceive no cause except play; he abhaya-āśraya — O refuge of fearlessness; he nitya-mukta — O eternally liberated Lord; jīvātmani api bhava-ādayaḥ — even in the individual self, birth and other conditions of becoming; tvayi viṣaye yā avidyā tayā kṛtāḥ — are produced by ignorance concerning You; na paramārthataḥ santi — they do not exist ultimately.
39.translation: Having spoken of the Lord’s ‘birth,’ the gods make clear that it is not birth under saṃsāra as in the case of an ordinary jīva. O Lord, O refuge of fearlessness, You are eternally free; no compulsory cause for Your birth can be conceived. Its only cause is Your play. Śrīdhara adds that even the jīva’s conditions of birth, maintenance and dissolution arise through ignorance of You and are not ultimate realities in themselves.

40.word_for_word: prastutaṃ prārthayante — they now state their immediate prayer; matsya-aśva iti — with the verse beginning ‘Matsya, Aśva…’; naḥ asmān — us; tri-bhuvanaṃ ca — and the three worlds; anyadā yathā pāsi — as You protected before; tathā adhunā api pāhi — protect us now as well; bhāraṃ bhuvaḥ hara — remove the burden of earth; vandanaṃ te iti vadantaḥ — saying ‘our obeisance to You’; sarve śirobhiḥ praṇamanti — all bow their heads.
40.translation: The gods now make their immediate prayer. Just as the Lord protected them and the three worlds in His previous descents, they ask Him to protect them now and remove the burden of the earth. Saying, ‘Our obeisance to You,’ they all bow their heads.

41.word_for_word: devakīṃ prati āhuḥ — they address Devakī; diṣṭyā — by great good fortune; naḥ asmākaṃ bhavāya udbhavāya — for our welfare and restoration; sākṣāt paraḥ pumān — the Supreme Person Himself; te kukṣiṃ gataḥ — has entered your womb; ataḥ bhayaṃ mā bhūt — therefore let there be no fear.
41.translation: The gods then address Devakī: ‘By great good fortune, the Supreme Person Himself has entered your womb for our welfare. Therefore do not be afraid.’

42.word_for_word: yasya rūpam anidam — whose form is ‘an-idam,’ not an external object; sarva-pratyag-bhūtam — present as the innermost Self of all; yathā — exactly; yathāvat — as it truly is; asmān vañcayitvā etau iha sthāsyete iti manyamānāḥ — thinking ‘these two might deceive us and remain here’; brahma-īśānau purodhāya — placing Brahmā and Īśāna in front; purataḥ kṛtvā — making them go first; yayuḥ — the gods departed.
42.translation: The Lord’s form is called ‘an-idam’: it is not merely an external object, for He is the innermost Self of all. ‘Yathā’ means ‘exactly as He truly is.’ The other gods, wary that Brahmā and Śiva might remain behind after sending them away, placed Brahmā and Īśāna at the front of the departing assembly and then returned to heaven.
